title: Join the middles of a square's sides: what shape is inside?
description: The midpoints of the sides of a square are joined in order, and the video asks what the inner figure is. It matches the four corner triangles, uses their forty five degree angles at each midpoint, and checks the drawing by measuring.
teaching_notes: One idea: the four corner triangles match, so the inner figure has four equal sides, and the angles at each midpoint leave a right angle. Watch for students who call the tilted figure a rhombus because it stands on its corner.

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 7)
video_script.why: The child uses the forty five degree angles of a right triangle with two equal sides to show that the inner figure has four equal sides and four right angles.
video_script.substitution: Show that the four corner triangles match, find their base angles as in the square with its diagonal, and take them from the straight angle at each midpoint.
video_script.anchor: square CASE with the midpoints U, V, W and X of its sides joined in order
video_script.payoff_line: The inner figure U V W X is a square

final_answer.value: UVWX is a square; four marks at equal distances from the corners, taken the same way round, also make a square
final_answer.spoken: the inner figure U V W X is a square

maths_rules: CASE is a square with U, V, W, X the midpoints of its sides in order; at each corner the two half sides are equal and the corner angle is 90 degrees
the four corner triangles match by SAS, so UV = VW = WX = XU
each corner triangle has two equal sides and a right angle, so its base angles are 45 degrees each
at a midpoint, 45 + 45 + angle of UVWX = 180, so the angle of UVWX = 180 - 45 - 45 = 90 degrees
UVWX has four equal sides and four right angles, so it is a square
four marks at the same distance from the corners, all going the same way round, give four matching right triangles, so another square
video_script.design: One idea: matching corner triangles give equal sides and 45 degree angles give right angles. The square with the inner figure stays on the board.
